title: American Investors Pour $3.4 Billion Into IPL With Two Record-Breaking Deals
excerpt: Kal Somani-led consortium acquires Rajasthan Royals for $1.63 billion while David Blitzer's group buys Royal Challengers Bengaluru for $1.78 billion, marking a watershed moment for Indian cricket's global reach.
body:
• Rajasthan Royals sold to Arizona-based Kal Somani's consortium, including Walmart, for $1.63 billion — a franchise that cost $67 million in 2008.
  • Royal Challengers Bengaluru acquired by David Blitzer's Bolt Ventures and Blackstone for $1.78 billion, the highest price ever paid for an IPL team.
  • Both deals closed on the same day, signaling a surge of American institutional capital into Indian sports at a time when cricket is set to return to the Olympics in 2028.

Two American-led consortiums have collectively spent more than $3.4 billion to acquire stakes in Indian Premier League franchises, shattering previous valuation records and underscoring the growing appeal of Indian cricket among global institutional investors.

The deals, both finalized on the same day, represent the first time IPL franchises have crossed the $1 billion threshold — and they did so twice in a matter of hours.

The Rajasthan Royals Deal

Kal Somani, an existing minority shareholder in the Rajasthan Royals based in Scottsdale, Arizona, led a consortium that includes Walmart to acquire 100 percent of the Jaipur-based franchise for $1.63 billion, approximately INR 16,290 crore.

Somani, in his 50s, has interests spanning technology, academia, and sports. He is one of the founders of Motor City Golf Club, which has an association with Tiger Woods. His son, Arjun Somani, is a promising player on the U.S. junior golf circuit.

The consortium is expected to take over from UK-based Manoj Badale of Emerging Media after the 2026 IPL season. The Board of Control for Cricket in India must still approve the transaction and will receive approximately INR 765 crore — five percent of the deal value — per the franchise agreement.

"The acquisition of Rajasthan Royals by a Kal Somani-led consortium at $1.63 billion reinforces our view that IPL franchises are now valued in the $1.5-2.0 billion range, supported by strong media monetisation and rising global investor interest."

— Karan Turani, Elara Capital

RCB Sets a New Record

That record lasted only hours. Reigning champion Royal Challengers Bengaluru was acquired for $1.78 billion by a consortium that includes U.S. billionaire David Blitzer's Bolt Ventures, American asset manager Blackstone, and the Aditya Birla Group.

Blitzer described the IPL as "one of the great growth stories in global sport." He already holds ownership stakes in the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers, the NHL's New Jersey Devils, and the English Premier League's Crystal Palace.

Kumar Mangalam Birla, chairman of the Aditya Birla Group, called RCB "one of the most compelling franchises in modern sport" and said the deal offers "a distinctive platform to extend our legacy into the arena of global sport." Aditya Birla director Aryaman Vikram Birla will serve as chairman of the new ownership group, with Satyan Gajwani of the Times of India Group as vice chairman.

"It's mind-boggling numbers. But great news for Indian cricket and the way forward. I think it's already as big as the NBA."

— Sourav Ganguly, former India cricket captain

A Massive Leap From 2008 Valuations

The scale of these transactions comes into sharp focus against the franchises' original price tags. When the IPL launched in 2008, liquor baron Vijay Mallya purchased RCB for $111.6 million, and Rajasthan sold for just $67 million. The current deals represent valuation increases of roughly 16-fold and 24-fold, respectively.

The IPL's broadcast rights for the 2023-27 cycle were sold for $6.4 billion to Disney Star and Reliance Viacom18, which have since combined to form JioStar. Two newer franchises, Gujarat Titans and Lucknow Super Giants, were added in 2021 for $670 million and $940 million.

Why American Money Is Flowing In

Several factors are driving U.S. investor interest. Cricket made a foray into the American market with the 2024 T20 World Cup, won by India, and the sport will feature at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Major League Cricket, a U.S.-based T20 competition launched in 2023, operates with the backing of IPL franchises — Chennai Super Kings, Kolkata Knight Riders, and Mumbai Indians all own MLC teams.

Walmart, part of Somani's consortium, already has significant India exposure through its majority stake in e-commerce giant Flipkart and its control of PhonePe, the country's leading digital payments platform. Rob Walton, the 81-year-old former Walmart chairman and eldest son of founder Sam Walton, is also an owner of the NFL's Denver Broncos.

Deloitte analysts have noted that the sports industry is "entering an age of expansion," with private equity deals across leagues jumping in recent years. The IPL, which runs just three months annually in its Twenty20 format, has become cricket's most lucrative property globally.
image_caption: A night cricket match at Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, India. American investors have poured over $3.4 billion into IPL franchises in two record-breaking deals.
nri_angle: The deals signal a growing convergence of American capital and Indian sport, with U.S.-based Indian-origin entrepreneurs and major corporations deepening their stakes in the country's cricket ecosystem.
